name: The Sloop Inn
description: A centuries-old harbourside inn with low beams and a proper Cornish welcome for dogs and walkers. The terrace looks straight over St Ives harbour, perfect for watching boats while you eat.

name: Godrevy Beach
description: A wide Atlantic beach beneath the National Trust headland where dogs can run and paddle all year round. Climb the cliff path for views across to Godrevy lighthouse, the inspiration for the novel To the Lighthouse.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Kynance Cove
description: A dazzling cove of white sand ringed by red-and-green serpentine rock stacks. The steep path down from the car park is the price of entry, but the space and scenery reward steady paws.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Porthcurno Beach
description: A sheltered golden cove beneath the open-air Minack Theatre, with calm shallows and soft sand. It fills up fast on summer days, so go early or out of season for room to throw a ball.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: South West Coast Path: Portreath to St Ives
description: A rollercoaster stretch of clifftop path linking two classic surfing towns, with engine houses, seal-spotting coves and endless sea views. Take water for both of you — it is tougher than it looks.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Driftwood Spars
description: A quirky pub built partly from ships' timbers, tucked in a valley right above Trevaunance Cove. Dogs get a bowl and a biscuit while you try the local ales and the famous fish pie.

name: Bossiney Beach
description: A hidden cove reached by steep steps, with a blowhole, a cave and usually plenty of space to yourself. One of the quieter North Cornwall beaches, ideal for off-lead exploring at low tide.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Ship Inn
description: A classic harbourside local tucked into Mousehole's narrow lanes, with a tiny bar that is always full of character and dogs. Settle in with a pint of local ale and watch the fishing boats at anchor.

name: Saunton Sands
description: Three miles of flat golden sand backed by the great dune system of Braunton Burrows, with room for dogs to race at full pelt. The surf here is lively, which is exactly what water-loving dogs want.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Woolacombe Beach
description: A wide Blue Flag bay with powerful surf and soft sand that swallows up a whole afternoon. Dogs are welcome on the main beach early and late in summer and all day the rest of the year.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Postbridge & the East Dart
description: An easy riverside loop on Dartmoor from the famous clapper bridge, with moorland ponies and granite tors on the skyline. There are plenty of shallow stretches for a paddle and a picnic.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Lydford Gorge
description: A National Trust gorge walk squeezed between dripping ferns and swirling river, ending at the 30-metre Whitelady Waterfall. The cliff path is narrow in places, so keep dogs on leads and watch your footing.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: North Devon Coast Path: Croyde to Baggy Point
description: A short, punchy clifftop circuit around Baggy Point with huge views over Croyde Bay and, on clear days, Lundy Island. Plenty of side gullies and sandy coves for a dog to investigate.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Globe Inn
description: A 16th-century coaching inn with a dog-friendly bar and a garden looking over the River Exe. It sits at the end of a lovely estuary walk, so you can earn your pint first.

name: The Masons Arms
description: A thatched, low-ceilinged inn in a picture-postcard village close to the Jurassic Coast. Dogs are welcome at the bar and in the garden, and the beach walk from the front door is a proper leg-stretcher.

name: The Anglers Rest
description: A friendly seafront pub with sea views, local ales and a menu big on fresh seafood. It is a short walk from two miles of sandy beach and the start of the South West Coast Path.

name: Catbells
description: The Lake District's favourite little fell — a steep, scrambly but short climb with one of the best views in the Lakes. Sturdy paws and boots will manage it, and the descent to the shore of Derwentwater is the reward.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Derwentwater Shore Path
description: A gentle, mostly flat lakeside path from Keswick around the wooded shore of Derwentwater. There are constant places to paddle, lakeside benches for the humans and not a steep step in sight.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Dog & Gun
description: A proper Lakeland boozer whose name says it all — muddy boots and damp dogs are part of the furniture. Expect real ales, big portions and a wood burner to dry off by after a day on the fells.

name: The Kirkstile Inn
description: A 16th-century inn at the foot of Mellbreak with its own microbrewery and a snug full of walkers' dogs. The flat circuit of Loweswater lake starts from the door, making it the classic pub-with-a-walk.

name: Wasdale Head & Wast Water Shore
description: A wild walk along the shore of England's deepest lake, with Scafell Pike towering at the head of the valley. The path is rough and the weather changes fast, so it suits sure-footed dogs and quiet walkers.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cockshott Point & Windermere Shore
description: An easy, flat shore walk from Bowness with far-reaching views across the widest part of Windermere. It is pushchair-friendly, full of stick-chasing potential and close to the town's dog-tolerant cafés.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: St Bees Beach
description: A long shingle-and-sand beach at the western start of the Wainwright Coast to Coast walk. Dogs can stretch their legs for miles beneath the red sandstone cliffs and the seabird colony above.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Drunken Duck
description: A famously good inn high above Windermere, brewing its own beer and serving serious Cumbrian food. Dogs get a warm welcome, a water bowl and usually a biscuit while you eat.

name: Robin Hood's Bay Beach
description: A sweeping, dog-friendly beach below the old fishing village of the same name. At low tide you can walk the firm sand south to the smugglers' caves and back with your toes in the water.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cleveland Way: Robin Hood's Bay to Whitby
description: A dramatic six-mile clifftop leg of the Cleveland Way between two of Yorkshire's best coastal towns. Keep an eye out for dolphins, and give the nesting seabirds some room below the cliffs.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Brimham Rocks
description: A surreal National Trust landscape of wind-carved gritstone towers where dogs can scramble between the rocks. The waymarked circular path takes in all the strangest formations, including the Dancing Bear.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Malham Cove & Gordale Scar
description: A classic Yorkshire Dales walk linking a 100-metre limestone amphitheatre with the dramatic gorge of Gordale Scar. There are steps, stiles and grazing sheep, so leads are the sensible choice.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Flamborough South Landing
description: A sheltered pebble beach beneath towering white chalk cliffs at the edge of Flamborough Head. Dogs love the rock pools at low tide, and the clifftop path offers a longer stroll above.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Fat Badger
description: A characterful pub beside Harrogate's Valley Gardens with a genuinely dog-friendly bar and a menu of Yorkshire classics. The gardens and pine woods out back are ideal for a pre-lunch walk.

name: The Ship Inn
description: A no-frills seafront pub a couple of minutes from Filey's long sandy beach. Expect cheap pints, big plates of fish and chips and a bar that is used to wet dogs.

name: Whitby Abbey Headland Route
description: A breezy clifftop loop around the abbey headland with sweeping views over Whitby's red roofs and harbour. The classic approach is the famous 199 steps up from the town, and dogs are welcome on leads.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Mam Tor & the Great Ridge
description: A classic ridge walk with 360-degree views from the 'shivering mountain' across the Edale and Hope valleys. Start from Castleton and reward the climb with a pint in one of the village pubs.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Dovedale Stepping Stones
description: A gentle walk along the River Dove to the famous stepping stones, framed by limestone crags and ancient woodland. The shallows are perfect for a dog to cool off, and there are several picnic spots.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Ladybower Reservoir Shore
description: A flat, easy path along the shore of the great Ladybower Reservoir with the dams and Derwent Edge above. Good for older dogs and prams, with plenty of benches and open water views.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bakewell Riverside Walk
description: A pretty town walk following the River Wye through meadows and past the 13th-century bridge. Finish with a Bakewell pudding — most of the town's cafés are happy to see well-behaved dogs.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Peacock at Rowsley
description: A smart country pub on the edge of the Peak District with a roaring fire and a proper welcome for dogs. Walk off the roast along the River Derwent or in the gardens after lunch.

name: The Old Hall Inn
description: A 17th-century coaching inn at the foot of the Pennines, popular with walkers and their dogs. Real fires, cask ales and a menu that does not mess about.

name: The Royal Oak
description: A classic stone-built pub on the old moorland turnpike road above the Staffordshire border. Dogs get a bowl and a fuss while walkers work through the excellent Sunday roasts.

name: Chatsworth Estate Parkland
description: A sweeping parkland walk around the Duke of Devonshire's estate, following the River Derwent past the famous house. Dogs must stay on leads, but the space, deer park and views make up for it.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Three Cliffs Bay
description: The postcard beach of the Gower Peninsula — a golden bay guarded by three sea stacks and a great dune system. There is no direct road access, so dogs get space and the walk in is half the fun.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Rhossili Bay
description: Three miles of unbroken sand beneath the whaleback of Rhossili Down, repeatedly voted one of the world's best beaches. Dogs can run the entire length of it, and the Worm's Head causeway is an adventure at low tide.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Llanberis Path up Snowdon
description: The gentlest of the main routes up Wales's highest mountain, following the old railway line for much of the way. It is still a full day out, so allow six hours and keep dogs on leads near grazing sheep.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Pen y Fan
description: The highest peak in south Wales, reached by a steady grassy climb from the Storey Arms car park. On a clear day the views stretch for miles, but the summit is busy — go early on a weekday.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Llyn Idwal & the Ogwen Valley
description: A dramatic lakeside circuit beneath the sheer cliffs of the Glyderau, with some of Snowdonia's most impressive mountain scenery. The path is well trodden but the weather can change in minutes, so pack waterproofs.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Pembrokeshire Coast Path: St David's to Whitesands
description: A glorious cliff-top stretch of the Pembrokeshire Coast Path past St Non's Chapel and St David's Head. Expect seabirds, wildflowers and, if you are lucky, porpoises playing in the bay below.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The White Horse
description: A relaxed pub with rooms in a pretty Black Mountains town, serving local ales and seasonal food. Dogs are welcome at the bar, and canal towpath and hill walks start right outside the door.

name: The West Arms
description: A 16th-century inn tucked in a quiet Ceiriog Valley village, all low beams, open fires and proper Welsh hospitality. The hills around are laced with quiet footpaths made for a post-lunch stroll.

name: Arthur's Seat
description: An ancient volcano in the middle of Edinburgh offering the city's best panorama. The main path up from Holyrood is wide and well graded, and the grassy summit makes a fine picnic spot.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Portobello Beach
description: Edinburgh's seaside — a long, gently shelving beach with the city skyline behind you. Dogs are welcome all year, and the Victorian promenade is lined with cafés and chippies for afterwards.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: St Andrews West Sands
description: The long flat beach made famous by Chariots of Fire, stretching for two miles beside the golf links. Firm sand at the water's edge is perfect for a gallop, and the Eden Estuary nature reserve is at the far end.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Loch an Eilein
description: A beautiful, easy circuit around a pine-fringed loch with a ruined island castle at its heart. The path is flat and pram-friendly, and there is a cafe with a view at the start.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Sheep Heid Inn
description: Claimed to be Scotland's oldest pub, hidden in the village of Duddingston at the foot of Arthur's Seat. Dogs get water and a fuss, and the ancient skittle alley is a proper curiosity.

name: The Old Bridge Inn
description: A cosy riverside pub in the heart of the Cairngorms with a famously deep whisky list. Dogs are welcome, and the Speyside trails and Loch an Eilein are a short stroll away.

name: Glenfinnan Viaduct Walk
description: An atmospheric walk around the head of Loch Shiel with the famous curved viaduct soaring overhead. Check the Jacobite steam train timetable so you are in position when it rumbles across the arches.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Canny Man's
description: A gloriously cluttered Morningside institution stacked with bric-a-brac, maps and whisky, famous for its dog-loving staff. It is small and busy, so treat it as a drink-and-a-snack stop rather than a big meal.

name: Causeway Coast Way: Portballintrae to the Giant's Causeway
description: A thrilling cliff-top stretch of the Causeway Coast Way with the Atlantic roaring into sea arches and blowholes below. The route links Portballintrae to the Giant's Causeway with huge views over to Scotland.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Giant's Causeway Coastal Path
description: The clifftop approach to the world-famous basalt columns, with seabird cliffs and sea-stack views along the way. Keep dogs on leads on the busy sections, but the Atlantic air is unbeatable.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Ballycastle Beach
description: A long sandy beach in a sheltered bay looking across to Rathlin Island and, on the clearest days, the Mull of Kintyre. The flat seafront promenade makes an easy evening stroll with the dog.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Fullerton Arms
description: A friendly town-centre pub known for its quirky carved wooden doors and hearty bar food. Dogs get a warm welcome, and the beach and Glens of Antrim walks are minutes away.

name: Crawfordsburn Beach
description: A sheltered sandy beach in a wooded glen on the shores of Belfast Lough. The country park's riverside paths are lovely for a longer walk, and there is plenty of room for dogs even in summer.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Dirty Duck Ale House
description: A proper ale house beside Holywood railway station, pouring cask beer and serving big plates of comfort food. Dogs are welcome, and the coastal path along Belfast Lough starts outside the door.

name: Howth Cliff Path
description: A stunning cliff loop around the Howth headland with Dublin Bay laid out behind you and sheep-dotted hillsides ahead. The full circuit takes a couple of hours, with plenty of spots to stop and watch the seals.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Sandycove & the Forty Foot
description: A classic Dublin swimming spot where bathers brave the water all year and dogs are welcome on the rocks and grass. The views across Dublin Bay to Howth are among the best on the coast.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Killiney Hill
description: A short, steep walk up Killiney Hill for one of the finest panoramas on Ireland's east coast — the 'Irish Riviera' of Killiney Bay lies below. There is an obelisk at the top and plenty of benches on the way.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Glendalough & the Wicklow Way
description: A beautiful lakeside walk from the ancient monastic city up into the Wicklow Mountains along the Wicklow Way. The lower lake loop is easy, and the climb to the upper lake is well worth the puff.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Greystones Beach
description: A long shingle-and-sand beach at the end of the popular cliff walk from Bray. Dogs can swim and run for miles, and the seafront has plenty of cafés for the humans.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Inchydoney Beach
description: Two connected strands of golden sand wrapping around a headland on the wild West Cork coast. One of Ireland's best dog beaches, with surf, dunes and the pubs of Clonakilty a short drive away.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Bleeding Horse
description: A warm Victorian-era pub on Camden Street with a proper welcome for dogs at the bar. It is a favourite for a post-walk pint, and the Grand Canal towpath is a five-minute stroll away.

name: The Abbey Tavern
description: A traditional Irish pub in the heart of Howth village, famous for seafood and live music. Dogs are welcome, and it is the perfect refuel stop at the end of the Howth cliff path.

name: Tehidy Country Park
description: Cornwall's largest country park, with 250 acres of woodland, lakes and wide grassy rides that dogs can explore off the lead. The network of surfaced paths makes it an easy morning walk in all weathers.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Mount Edgcumbe Country Park
description: Grade I listed parkland at the mouth of the River Tamar with sweeping lawns, woodland and views across Plymouth Sound. Dogs are welcome throughout, and the coastal path from the gardens is superb.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bodmin Beacon
description: A restored hillside parkland crowned by the landmark beacon tower above Bodmin town. Wide, open grass slopes and woodland paths give dogs plenty of room to run with the town laid out below.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Trelissick Estate
description: A National Trust estate of parkland and riverside woods on a bend of the Fal estuary. Dogs are welcome on leads in the gardens and can enjoy the woods and shoreline paths too.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Stover Country Park
description: A peaceful country park built around a grand lake, with heathland, woods and plenty of duck-watching. There is a level dog-friendly route around the water and a cafe at the old gatehouse.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Parke Estate
description: A National Trust estate of wood pasture and parkland on the edge of Dartmoor, with a riverside walk along the River Bovey. Dogs can stretch out on the open lawns or follow the estate's waymarked trails.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Killerton Estate
description: A National Trust estate with sweeping parkland, formal gardens and miles of woodland paths. Dogs are welcome on the estate walks (on leads in the gardens) and there is space for a long afternoon.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Dartington Estate
description: A thousand-acre estate of parkland, ancient woodland and gardens around the historic Dartington Hall. Dogs are welcome on the estate trails, with the River Dart running along one side.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Brockhole
description: The Lake District Visitor Centre on the shores of Windermere, with terraced gardens, lawns and lake-shore paths. It is a relaxed, easy-to-reach spot with a cafe, and dogs are welcome throughout.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Whinlatter Forest Park
description: England's only true mountain forest, with miles of wide forest tracks that are brilliant for off-lead running. The red squirrel viewpoint and the cafe make it a full day out for two and four legs.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Fell Foot
description: A National Trust lakeside park at the southern tip of Windermere with sweeping lawns running down to the water. Dogs are welcome all year, and the boathouse cafe is a handy refuel stop.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Grizedale Forest
description: A working forest packed with sculpture trails, lakes and quiet tracks where dogs can roam for hours. The visitor centre has a cafe, and the mountain-bike trails mean you can mix up the day.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Stray
description: Two hundred acres of open, unfenced grassland right in the middle of Harrogate, criss-crossed by wide paths. Dogs can have a proper run in the centre of town, with a cafe at each corner.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Valley Gardens
description: Fifty acres of woodland and streamside gardens running through the heart of Harrogate. Paved paths, a boating lake and plenty of sniffing opportunities make it a firm favourite with local dog walkers.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Rowntree Park
description: A Victorian park beside the River Ouse with lawns, woodland and a lake, all within walking distance of York city centre. The riverside path links it to the Millennium Bridge for a longer loop.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Dalby Forest
description: A huge Forestry England forest on the slopes of the North York Moors with miles of family-friendly trails. There is a dog-friendly zone on the red route and a cafe at the visitor centre.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Markeaton Park
description: Derby's most popular park, with open lawns, woodland, a river and a great playground. The circular paths are flat and easy, and there are plenty of benches and two cafés.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Elvaston Castle Country Park
description: A romantic Gothic-revival estate with wildflower meadows, woodland and a lake beside the castle ruins. Dogs are welcome across the park, and the formal gardens are worth a look too.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Buxton Pavilion Gardens
description: A beautiful Victorian park in the middle of Buxton with the River Wye flowing through it. Tree-lined avenues, a bandstand and the opera house backdrop make it a lovely town-centre dog stroll.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Shipley Country Park
description: Nearly 800 acres of parkland, lakes and old pit mounds on the edge of the Amber Valley. There are miles of multi-user trails and a great cafe in the old stables courtyard.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bute Park
description: Cardiff's green heart — 130 acres of parkland, gardens and river walk alongside the castle. Dogs are welcome on leads, with the Taff Trail running along one side for a longer outing.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Roath Park
description: A much-loved Cardiff park with a huge boating lake, tree-lined promenade and a glasshouse at the top. The lake walk is flat and pushchair-friendly, and the botanical gardens next door are beautiful.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Margam Country Park
description: A grand country estate with 1,000 acres of parkland, the ruins of Margam Abbey and herds of deer. Dogs are welcome throughout the park, and the orangery cafe is worth seeking out.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bryngarw Country Park
description: A beautiful wooded parkland in the Garw Valley with the river running through the middle. There are circular waymarked walks, a walled garden and plenty of shady spots for warm days.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Meadows
description: Edinburgh's favourite flat green space — a mile-long stretch of open grassland perfect for a dog to stretch its legs. The paths are busy with runners and cyclists, but the open centre is all yours.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Pollok Country Park
description: Glasgow's largest park, with 360 acres of woodland, the Burrell Collection and free-roaming Highland cattle. Keep dogs under close control near the cows, but otherwise it is off-lead heaven.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Dalkeith Country Park
description: A historic estate with a riverside adventure trail, walled garden and miles of woodland paths. The Fort Douglas play area and cafe make it a firm favourite with families and their dogs.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Vogrie Country Park
description: A friendly country park in Midlothian with mature woodland, the River Tyne and a great adventure playground. The walled garden and easy circular paths make it an all-weather favourite.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Ormeau Park
description: Belfast's oldest public park, a long stretch of mature trees and open lawns along the River Lagan. The Lagan towpath links it to the city centre for a longer riverside walk.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Belvoir Park Forest
description: A mature forest of 80 hectares on the edge of south Belfast with beautiful old beech and oak avenues. The waymarked trails wind through the woods with the river nearby and very few crowds.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Carnfunnock Country Park
description: A coastal country park on the Antrim Coast Road with woodland, a walled garden and sea views across to Scotland. The maze and adventure playground keep everyone busy, and dogs are welcome.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Phoenix Park
description: One of the largest enclosed city parks in Europe, with 1,750 acres of grassland, woods and the famous wild deer. It is a true escape from the city — just keep dogs well away from the deer.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: St Anne's Park
description: A huge public park on Dublin's northside with woodlands, a rose garden, playing fields and a lovely cafe in the old stables. The weekend food market is a local highlight.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Marlay Park
description: A popular south Dublin park with a historic house, craft courtyard, farmers' market and riverside walks. There are designated dog-friendly areas and plenty of space on the open lawns.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bushy Park
description: A beautiful park in Terenure with the River Dodder running along one side and a tree-lined avenue at its heart. It is smaller than Phoenix Park but full of character and much-loved by local dog walkers.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Glen River Park
description: A hidden gem of a woodland park on Cork city's north side, following the Glen River through mature trees. It feels a world away from the city, with steep but rewarding paths.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Pandora Inn
description: A whitewashed inn on the edge of Restronguet Creek with a pontoon garden right on the water. It is one of Cornwall's classic dog-friendly pubs, with mooring views and seafood to match.

name: The Rock Inn
description: A granite inn on the edge of Dartmoor with a roaring fire and a proper welcome for wet dogs. The lane up to Haytor Rocks starts outside, so you can earn your pint first.

name: The Nobody Inn
description: A centuries-old inn hidden in a tiny Dartmoor village, famous for its huge wine cellar and cream teas. Dogs are welcome by the fire, and the lanes around are perfect for a wander.

name: The Wild Boar
description: A grand old coaching inn with its own golf club and a cosy, dog-friendly bar. It sits on the edge of the Winster Valley, with lovely country lanes for a pre-dinner walk.

name: The Mortal Man
description: A much-loved Lakeland inn in the hilltop village of Troutbeck, with a long dog-friendly history. The views across to the fells from the beer garden are among the best in the Lakes.

name: The Fox & Hounds
description: A warm village pub on the edge of the North York Moors, welcoming walkers and their dogs all year. The open fires and home-cooked food are the reward for a day on the heather.

name: The Chequers Inn
description: A cosy stone inn in the Hope Valley with a streamside garden and a menu of proper pub food. Dogs are welcome throughout, and the walk to Froggatt Edge starts from the door.

name: The Three Stags' Heads
description: A famously traditional pub high on the Derbyshire hills with no bar — beers are pulled from the cellar and brought to your table. Dogs are welcome in the snug, and the views are huge.

name: The Old Black Lion
description: A 17th-century coaching inn in the book town of Hay-on-Wye, with a dog-friendly bar and rooms. It is a short walk from the castle and the River Wye, and the Sunday roasts are legendary.

name: The Felin Fach Griffin
description: A celebrated country inn at the foot of the Brecon Beacons with a proper dog welcome and top-notch seasonal food. The owners keep a barrel of dog biscuits behind the bar.

name: The Hanging Bat
description: A craft-beer bar in the West End with a genuinely dog-friendly room and a wood-fired kitchen. There are always a few well-behaved dogs under the tables, and the staff bring water bowls without asking.

name: The Bridge Inn
description: A riverside inn on the Union Canal with a famously dog-friendly bar and a big waterside terrace. The canal towpath runs right past the door for a relaxed pre- or post-pint stroll.

name: The Gravediggers
description: Officially John Kavanagh's, but everyone knows it as The Gravediggers — a perfect Victorian pub beside Glasnevin Cemetery. Traditional snug, proper pints and a warm welcome for dogs.

name: Harlyn Bay
description: A sheltered family beach just west of Padstow with soft sand and gentle waves. Dogs are welcome all year, and the dunes behind are a great place for an evening zoom.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bantham Beach
description: A long stretch of golden sand at the mouth of the River Avon, with surf and stunning views up the estuary. Dogs are welcome all year on most of the beach, and the village pub is dog-friendly.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Instow Beach
description: A gently shelving beach beside the Torridge estuary with calm, shallow water that suits paddle-loving dogs. The old railway line behind is now a flat, buggy-friendly walk.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Silecroft Beach
description: A long, quiet shingle-and-sand beach at the foot of Black Combe, with the fells rising straight behind. It is one of Cumbria's best beaches for an off-lead run with barely another soul around.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Runswick Bay
description: A sweeping, dog-friendly bay below a pretty cliff-top village with colourful cottages. At low tide the sand goes on for miles, and fossil hunters will be in heaven.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cayton Bay
description: A wide bay backed by grassy cliffs, popular with surfers and dog walkers alike. The walk down is steep, but the space and the sea make it worth every step.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Newgale Beach
description: A huge expanse of sand at the northern end of St Bride's Bay, famous for its beachfront pub and powerful surf. Dogs are welcome all year across most of the beach.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Oxwich Bay
description: A perfect crescent of golden sand in a sheltered bay on the south Gower coast. The dunes behind are a nature reserve and the whole bay is a brilliant, spacious dog beach.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Aberdour Silver Sands
description: A gentle, sheltered beach on the Fife coast with soft sand and shallow water. The railway station is a five-minute walk away, making it an easy day trip from Edinburgh.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Yellowcraig Beach
description: A wide, dune-backed beach near North Berwick with views across to Fidra island and its lighthouse. There is a small car park, a nature trail and plenty of room for dogs to race about.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Benone Beach
description: Seven miles of flat golden sand at the foot of Mussenden Temple, one of Northern Ireland's longest beaches. The open, exposed stretch is perfect for a bracing winter walk with the dog.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Portstewart Strand
description: A two-mile National Trust strand backed by high dunes at the mouth of the River Bann. There is a lovely walk through the dunes, and the beach is a firm favourite with dog owners.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Portmarnock Beach
description: The Velvet Strand — three miles of wide, firm sand just north of Dublin, famous from the opening line of a classic novel. Dogs can gallop along the water's edge with Howth Head on the horizon.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Brittas Bay
description: A two-mile stretch of soft golden sand backed by dunes, one of Ireland's best-loved family beaches. The open shoreline gives dogs plenty of room even on summer weekends.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bedruthan Steps & Carnewas
description: A dramatic National Trust clifftop path above a string of sea stacks that only appear at low tide. The steps down to the beach are steep, but the views along the coast are unforgettable.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Exe Estuary Trail
description: A flat, traffic-free cycle and walking path circling the whole Exe Estuary, with birdlife and water views all the way. Pick a section from Exmouth or Topsham for an easy, pram-friendly outing.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Wistman's Wood
description: A hauntingly ancient oak wood on the slopes of Dartmoor, with gnarled trees and boulders wrapped in moss. The moorland walk in is open and wild — keep dogs close where sheep graze.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Aira Force & Ullswater
description: A National Trust woodland gorge walk to a spectacular 65-foot waterfall on the Ullswater shore. The paths are well made but steep in places, and the lake views on the return leg are superb.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Roseberry Topping
description: The 'Yorkshire Matterhorn' — a distinctive sugarloaf hill with a short, sharp climb and huge views over the moors. The circular walk from Newton-under-Roseberry is a classic.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Kilburn White Horse & Sutton Bank
description: A ridge-top walk past the famous chalk white horse with views across the Vale of York. The escarpment path and the visitor centre cafe make it a brilliant half-day out.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cromford Canal Towpath
description: A flat, easy towpath walk along the old Cromford Canal past mills, woodland and the famous Leawood pumping house. It links Matlock and Cromford and is perfect for dogs of all ages.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Monsal Trail
description: A traffic-free route along a former railway line with five tunnels and the spectacular Monsal Head viaduct. Flat, well-surfaced and brilliant for dogs, bikes and buggies alike.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Stanage Edge
description: A wild gritstone escarpment above Hathersage with one of the finest ridgelines in the Peak District. The clifftop path is open and breezy, with endless room for a dog to run.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Elan Valley
description: A landscape of Victorian dams and reservoirs surrounded by hills and forest in mid-Wales. The trails around the lakes are family-friendly and the visitor centre is a great stopping point.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Loch Morlich
description: A glorious circuit around a pine-fringed loch with a sandy beach and views up to the Cairngorm summits. The flat path is easy going, and there are plenty of spots for a paddle break.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Murlough Nature Reserve
description: A 6,000-year-old sand dune system along the edge of Dundrum Bay, managed by the National Trust. The waymarked trails through the dunes are beautiful, with dogs welcome on leads.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cliffs of Moher Coastal Walk
description: One of Ireland's most dramatic walks, along the clifftops between Doolin and the visitor centre. Keep dogs on leads and a firm grip on the wind — the views over the Atlantic are phenomenal.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bray to Greystones Cliff Walk
description: A spectacular cliff path along the coast between two seaside towns, with the Irish Sea on one side and green hills on the other. Allow two to three hours and reward yourselves with tea at the end.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Holkham Beach
description: Four miles of wild, sandy beach backed by pine forest and dunes — one of England's most famous dog beaches. Dogs are welcome all year and there is room for a whole day of running.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Brancaster Beach
description: A wide stretch of firm sand and mudflats on the North Norfolk coast, popular with dog walkers and seal spotters. The beach huts and the famous Crab Hut make it a proper day out.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Wells-next-the-Sea Beach
description: A vast beach hidden behind the pine woods, with rows of colourful beach huts and the sea a long walk away at low tide. Dogs can run for miles along the firmer sand.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Norfolk Coast Path: Holkham to Wells
description: A flat, breezy stretch of the Norfolk Coast Path along the top of the dunes between Holkham Gap and Wells. The views over the marshland and out to sea are worth every step.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Anchor
description: A proper coastal pub in a tiny quayside village, famous for its fresh seafood and the seals on the nearby sandbanks. Dogs get a warm welcome by the fire after a walk along the coast.

name: Felbrigg Estate
description: A National Trust estate with a grand 17th-century house, walled garden and miles of woods and parkland. Dogs are welcome on the estate trails, with plenty of autumn colour to explore.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Southwold Beach
description: A classic seaside beach with colourful beach huts and the pier and lighthouse behind. The main beach has seasonal dog restrictions, but the areas at either end stay open for four-legged friends.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Dunwich Heath
description: A beautiful stretch of heathland and cliff-top paths on the Suffolk coast, run by the National Trust. The dunes, birdlife and the atmospheric ruined priory nearby make it a wonderful walk.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Crown
description: A boutique coastal inn in the heart of Southwold with a dog-friendly bar and rooms. Adnams beer, open fires and a short walk to the beach and pier.

name: Knettishall Heath
description: A wild heathland on the Norfolk-Suffolk border where the Little Ouse river begins. It is a haven for wildlife, and the circular walks through heather and woodland are lovely and quiet.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Camber Sands
description: Five miles of sand dunes and open beach — the only sandy beach in East Sussex. Dogs are banned from the main area in summer but welcome on the rest of the beach all year.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Seven Sisters Country Park
description: The famous chalk cliffs of the Seven Sisters rising above the River Cuckmere. The clifftop walk and the meandering river trail are superb, with dogs welcome on leads.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cuckmere Haven
description: A wild shingle beach at the mouth of the Cuckmere river, right below the Seven Sisters cliffs. It is one of the most photographed spots on the south coast and brilliant for a bracing walk.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The George Inn
description: A 600-year-old coaching inn at the top of the pretty village of Alfriston, with a dog-friendly bar and garden. The South Downs Way passes right through the village.

name: Ashdown Forest
description: The real Hundred Acre Wood — 6,500 acres of heathland and woodland where dogs can run off-lead for hours. The views from the high points across the Weald are glorious.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Botany Bay
description: A sandy cove with towering chalk stacks and sea caves — the most dramatic beach on the Isle of Thanet. Dogs are welcome, and there is a clifftop walk and a pub at the top.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Kingsgate Bay
description: A quieter neighbour of Botany Bay with a broad sandy beach below the clifftop Captain Digby pub. Dogs can explore the caves and rock pools at low tide.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: White Cliffs of Dover
description: The iconic white cliffs rising 100 metres above the Channel. The clifftop path from the visitor centre to South Foreland Lighthouse is open, windswept and unforgettable.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Bedgebury National Pinetum
description: A Forestry England pinetum with one of the finest collections of conifers in the world. The lakeside walks and open glades are great for dogs on leads, and the Go Ape course keeps the kids busy.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Westonbirt Arboretum
description: A world-famous arboretum with 15,000 trees from across the globe and spectacular autumn colour. Dogs are welcome on leads, and there are miles of quiet, level paths.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Crickley Hill
description: A National Trust hillfort on the edge of the Cotswold escarpment with huge views over the Severn Valley. The short cliff-top circular walk is a firm favourite with local dog walkers.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cotswold Way: Dovers Hill to Broadway Tower
description: A classic leg of the Cotswold Way from Dovers Hill down to the folly of Broadway Tower. The views over the Vale of Evesham are immense and the path is well-trodden.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Bell at Sapperton
description: A much-loved country pub tucked in a quiet Cotswold valley, run by the same family for generations. Dogs are welcome, and the garden and the lanes around are perfect for a stroll.

name: Ainsdale Beach
description: A wide, wild beach on the Sefton coast backed by the pine woods and dunes of Ainsdale National Nature Reserve. Dogs are welcome all year and there is space to run for miles.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Inn at Whitewell
description: A historic riverside inn in the Forest of Bowland with roaring fires, an outstanding wine cellar and a proper welcome for dogs. The River Hodder runs past the door.

name: Beacon Fell Country Park
description: A small but lovely country park on a hill above the Ribble Valley with panoramic views from the top. The woodland trails are great for dogs and there is a visitor centre with a cafe.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Lancaster Canal Towpath
description: A flat, peaceful towpath walk along the Lancaster Canal between the city and the countryside. Swans, herons and the occasional narrowboat make it an easy, relaxing outing.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Inch Beach
description: Three miles of golden sand on the Dingle Peninsula, one of Ireland's most spectacular beaches. Surfers, horse riders and dogs all share the space, with the mountain backdrop all around.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Rossbeigh Beach
description: A huge, ever-changing spit of sand at the head of Dingle Bay with views of the mountains across the water. Dogs can run for miles along the firm sand at low tide.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Muckross Lake Walk
description: A gentle lakeshore trail in Killarney National Park beneath the MacGillycuddy's Reeks. Red deer and rare woodland birds are the reward, and dogs should stay on leads near the deer.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Fanore Beach
description: A wild, unspoilt beach at the edge of the Burren where the rocky limestone meets the Atlantic. It is one of the best dog beaches in the west of Ireland, quiet even in summer.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Lahinch Beach
description: A lively surfing beach in a classic Irish seaside town, with the Burren hills behind. Dogs are welcome outside the main summer season and there are plenty of cafes for afterwards.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Mullaghmore Burren Walk
description: A loop around Mullaghmore, the landmark limestone hill in the heart of the Burren. The walk crosses flower-filled pavement and turloughs, with views of Galway Bay.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Portrush East Strand
description: Two miles of golden sand east of Portrush with dunes and a golf links behind. Dogs are welcome here all year, making it the pick of the Portrush beaches.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Castlewellan Forest Park
description: A forest park around a large lake with a famous walled garden and the world's biggest hedge. The woodland and lakeshore paths are great for dogs, and there is bike and boat hire on site.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Torr Head Coastal Walk
description: A wild clifftop path on the north Antrim coast with views across to Scotland's Mull of Kintyre. It is remote, rugged and wonderful — take supplies and keep dogs close to the cliff edge.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Dollymount Strand (Bull Island)
description: A long stretch of beach on the man-made Bull Island nature reserve in Dublin Bay. Dogs are welcome, and the views of the city skyline and Howth Head are superb.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Malahide Castle Demesne
description: A grand castle estate on Dublin's coast with 260 acres of parkland, woodland and a fairy trail. The walled garden and lakeside paths are lovely, and dogs are welcome throughout.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Hermitage of Braid
description: A peaceful valley walk along the Braid Burn with woodland and waterfalls in the middle of the city. The river and the narrow gorge make it a favourite with local dog owners.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Ogmore-by-Sea
description: A long stretch of sand at the mouth of the River Ogmore, with the ruined Ogmore Castle just upstream. Dogs are welcome and there is a great walk along the clifftop path.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cosmeston Lakes
description: A country park around two lakes in the Vale of Glamorgan, with a reconstructed medieval village nearby. The flat, circular paths are perfect for an easy walk with the dog.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Saltwick Bay
description: A quieter, dog-friendly bay just south of Whitby, famous for its fossil-rich cliffs and shipwreck tales. The climb down from the clifftop path is worth it for the space at low tide.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Scar House Reservoir
description: A dramatic walk around one of the great Nidderdale reservoirs, with the moors rising all around. It is remote and quiet, with big skies and the dam wall at one end.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Birch Hall Inn
description: A tiny two-room pub by a stream in the village of Beck Hole, near the steam railway at Goathland. It is famously dog-friendly and the pies are legendary.

name: Rydal Water Circular
description: A gentle circuit around one of the smallest and loveliest lakes, past Rydal Caves and the former home of William Wordsworth. Flat, easy and full of spots for a paddle.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: The Watering Hole
description: Cornwall's only pub sitting directly on the sand, right on Perranporth beach. Dogs are welcome, and you can watch the surf while you eat your lunch with your feet in the sand.

name: Croyde Beach
description: A famous surfing beach at the foot of a pretty village, with golden sand and dramatic surf. Dogs are welcome before and after the summer season on the main beach, and the dunes offer space all year.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Heddon Valley
description: A deep wooded valley on the Exmoor coast, run by the National Trust, with a river walk to the sea at Heddon's Mouth. The scenery is dramatic and the waterfall is a proper reward.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Derwent Edge
description: A wild gritstone ridge high above Ladybower Reservoir with a line of bizarre rock formations. The clifftop walk from Fairholmes is open and exhilarating with huge views.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Camusdarach Beach
description: The silver-sand beach made famous by the film Local Hero, near Morar in the west Highlands. The turquoise water and white sand make it one of Scotland's most beautiful beaches, and dogs love it.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Beddgelert Forest
description: A forest park in the heart of Snowdonia where the rivers Glaslyn and Colwyn meet. The riverside trails are gentle and there is a cafe by the entrance.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Walberswick Beach
description: A quiet, characterful beach with a boardwalk through the reeds and views across to Southwold pier. Dogs are welcome and the village's fish and chips are the best on the coast.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Sandringham Country Park
description: The Royal Family's country estate, with beautiful parkland full of mature oaks and a huge lake. The waymarked trails are superb and dogs are welcome throughout the country park.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Glenariff Forest Park
description: The 'Queen of the Glens' — a deep valley with a spectacular waterfall walk through native oak woodland. The tearoom and well-made paths make it an easy day for all ages.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Fair Head
description: A dramatic cliff plateau rising 200 metres above Murlough Bay, with panoramic views across to Rathlin. The clifftop path is exposed, so keep dogs close and enjoy the huge skies.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Slemish Mountain
description: The volcanic plug where St Patrick is said to have tended sheep, rising steeply from the Antrim countryside. The climb is short but steep, with superb views over the whole plateau.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: White Rocks Beach
description: A sheltered sandy cove backed by white chalk cliffs, close to the ruins of Dunluce Castle. Dogs are welcome, and there is a great clifftop path above the beach.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Blackhead Path
description: A clifftop coastal path from Whitehead to the lighthouse at Blackhead, with views across Belfast Lough. The route is popular with dog walkers and seal spotters alike.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Antrim Castle Gardens
description: Restored 17th-century gardens beside the Six Mile Water, with parterres, a long canal and the Clotworthy House tearooms. Dogs are welcome on leads among the clipped hedges.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Crumlin Glen
description: A wooded gorge walk along the Six Mile Water with waterfalls and mossy paths. It feels far wilder than its location on the edge of the village.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Carnmoney Hill
description: A wooded hill above Belfast Lough with waymarked trails and fine views over the city. A firm favourite with local dog walkers for a quick after-work leg-stretch.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Tollymore Forest Park
description: The grand gateway to the Mourne Mountains, with the Shimna River running through the forest. Gothic bridges, red deer and waymarked trails make it a classic.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Silent Valley
description: A dramatic reservoir in the heart of the Mournes, ringed by granite summits. The walk around the water is atmospheric and the visitor centre is excellent.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Rostrevor Forest
description: A steep, beautiful forest with the Fairy Glen at its foot and huge views over Carlingford Lough from the top. The old oak trees are among the oldest in Ireland.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Tyrella Beach
description: A Blue Flag sandy beach that slopes gently into Dundrum Bay. Dogs are welcome outside the summer season on the main beach, and there is plenty of space for a run.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Delamont Country Park
description: A family-friendly country park on the shores of Strangford Lough with woods, lakes and a great play area. The circular walks are flat and easy.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Scrabo Country Park
description: A hilltop park above Newtownards crowned by the 19th-century Scrabo Tower. The views across Strangford Lough are superb and the paths suit all abilities.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Gosford Forest Park
description: A mix of parkland and dense conifer forest around the ruined Gosford Castle. The waymarked trails pass a lake and an avenue of old trees, with dogs welcome throughout.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Palace Demesne
description: A beautiful public park around the former Archbishop's palace, with lakes, a walled garden and mature trees. The flat paths are ideal for a gentle dog walk.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Gortin Glen Forest Park
description: A scenic forest park in the Sperrin Mountains with a lake, viewpoint and waymarked trails. The panoramic views over the Tyrone hills are the main event.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Drum Manor Forest Park
description: A quiet forest park with a butterfly garden, a small lake and woodland walks. It is a peaceful, underrated spot for an off-lead stretch.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Castle Archdale Country Park
description: A large country park on the shores of Lower Lough Erne with woodland, a marina and wartime history. The flat lakeside paths are perfect for dogs.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Lough Navar Forest
description: A forest drive high above Lower Lough Erne with the famous 'Cliffs' viewpoint. The views over the lakelands are among the best in Fermanagh.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Florence Court
description: A National Trust estate with parkland, woods and the famous Irish Yew tree. Dogs are welcome on the estate walks and there is plenty of room to roam.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Downhill Beach
description: A huge, dramatic beach below Mussenden Temple, stretching for miles towards the Bann mouth. Dogs can run the whole length, with the clifftop temple looking down.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Ness Country Park
description: A deep wooded glen with a chain of waterfalls along the River Ness. The paths are steep in places but the scenery is spectacular.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Binevenagh
description: A flat-topped mountain with a viewpoint over Lough Foyle and the Roe Valley. The open summit has huge skies and is wonderfully quiet.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Cave Hill Country Park
description: The dramatic basalt cliffs behind Belfast Castle, including the famous 'Napoleon's Nose'. The summit walk offers the best panorama of the city and the lough.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Stormont Estate
description: The sweeping parkland around Parliament Buildings, with mature trees and grand views over the city. The open lawns are popular with local dog walkers.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Dogs Bay
description: A horseshoe bay of rare white coral sand on the Connemara coast. The turquoise water and the island views make it one of Ireland's most beautiful beaches.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Gurteen Bay
description: A wild, sweeping beach right next to Dogs Bay with the Twelve Bens behind. Dogs can run for miles on the firm sand at low tide.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Connemara National Park
description: Over 2,000 hectares of mountains and moorland, with the Diamond Hill loop the classic walk. Keep dogs on leads near the free-roaming ponies and sheep.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Kylemore Abbey Grounds
description: The stunning lakeside estate of Kylemore Abbey with walled gardens and woodland walks. Dogs are welcome in the grounds on leads.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Barna Woods
description: A quiet woodland of ancient beech and oak on the outskirts of Galway city. The riverside paths are lovely for an easy walk with the dog.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Keem Bay
description: A stunning blue-flag cove at the end of the road on Achill Island, sheltered by high cliffs. The water is famously clear and dogs love the beach.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Old Head Beach
description: A wide Atlantic beach with views over Clew Bay and Croagh Patrick. There is room to run for miles, and the surf is often good.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Wild Nephin National Park
description: Ireland's wildest national park, with miles of remote bog and mountain trails. It is one of the darkest places in Europe, and gloriously quiet.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Rosses Point Beach
description: A lovely sandy beach with views over to Benbulben and the 'Metal Man' figure on the headland. Dogs are welcome and there is a classic seaside village behind.
opening_hours: Open all year — outdoor space, usually dawn to dusk.

name: Streedagh Beach
description: Three miles of sand where the wrecked Spanish Armada galleons lie offshore. It is a wild, beautiful beach with huge skies and plenty of space.
